description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol allows privileged clients such as the desktop control
center to configure user-level appearance settings managed by the
compositor, including cursor theme and size, fonts, and visual theming
(icon theme, accent color, window opacity, color scheme, titlebar height,
and corner radius).

This protocol is privileged. Binding it without compositor-level
authorization may result in requests being silently ignored or the
connection being terminated.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

A singleton privileged global for modifying user-level appearance
settings of the current user. These settings are shared by all
windows and clients of the user rather than being per-window.
Settings take effect immediately when a set_* request is sent.
The compositor applies each change and broadcasts the new value
to all clients bound to treeland_appearance_v1.

Set the cursor theme name. The compositor applies
the change immediately and broadcasts a cursor_theme event to
all active appearance observers. If the requested theme is
empty or not installed, the compositor falls back to a
default cursor theme.

args.name: name
args.summary: cursor theme name as recognized by the cursor theme subsystem

description.text:
Set the cursor size in pixels. Width and height
are specified independently to accommodate hardware cursor
planes that support non-square sizes. The compositor applies
the change immediately and broadcasts a cursor_size event to
all active appearance observers. Values of 0 or exceeding
compositor limits are clamped to the minimum or maximum
supported size.

Set the proportional font family. The compositor
applies the change immediately and broadcasts a font event to
all active appearance observers. If the requested font family
is empty or not installed, the compositor falls back to a
default font.

Set the monospace font family. The compositor
applies the change immediately and broadcasts a monospace_font
event to all active appearance observers. If the requested font
family is empty or not installed, the compositor falls back to
a default monospace font.

Set the base font size. The value is in points multiplied by
10, so 105 means 10.5 points. The compositor applies the change
immediately and broadcasts a font_size event to all active
appearance observers. A size of 0 or exceeding compositor
limits is clamped to the minimum or maximum supported size.

args.name: size
args.summary: font size in points multiplied by 10

description.text:
Set the icon theme name. The compositor applies
the change immediately and broadcasts an icon_theme event to
all active appearance observers. If the specified theme is
empty or not installed, the compositor falls back to a
default icon theme or ignores the change.

Set the accent color used for window
decorations, focus indicators, and compositor UI elements.

Color components are unsigned values in the range [0, 255].
The compositor handles out-of-range values according to its
own policy and may clamp a component to a supported bound.

The compositor applies the change immediately and broadcasts
an accent_color event to all active appearance observers.

Set the global window background opacity as a fixed-point
value in the range [0.0, 1.0]. A value of 1.0 means fully
opaque; 0.0 means fully transparent. The compositor handles
out-of-range values according to its own policy and may clamp
a value to a supported bound.

The compositor applies the change immediately and broadcasts
a window_opacity event to all active appearance observers.
description.summary: set the global window background opacity

description.text:
Set the color scheme hint. Values outside the color_scheme
enum range are silently ignored; the current color scheme
is kept unchanged.

The compositor applies the change immediately, updates
server-side decorations, and broadcasts a color_scheme event
to all active appearance observers so that clients can
restyle their self-drawn components.

Set the height of the compositor-drawn titlebar in pixels.
A value of 0 hides the compositor titlebar. The compositor
handles out-of-range values according to its own policy and
may clamp a value to a supported bound.

The compositor applies the change immediately and broadcasts
a titlebar_height event to all active appearance observers.

args.name: height
args.summary: titlebar height in pixels; 0 to hide titlebar

description.text:
Set the global default corner radius applied to window
decorations in pixels. This is the default for all windows;
individual windows may override it via
treeland_decoration_context_v1.set_corner_radius.
A value of 0 specifies square (unrounded) corners. The
compositor handles out-of-range values according to its own
policy and may clamp a value to a supported bound.

The compositor applies the change immediately and broadcasts
a corner_radius event to all active appearance observers.
description.summary: set the global window corner radius

args.name: radius
args.summary: corner radius in pixels; 0 for square corners

description.text:
A user-level hint for the preferred color scheme. Clients
should use this value to style their self-drawn widgets and
UI elements accordingly. The compositor also applies this
hint to server-side decorations. This is semantically
equivalent to org.freedesktop.appearance color-scheme and
the CSS prefers-color-scheme media feature.

This enum mirrors treeland_appearance_v1.color_scheme
(in the read-only treeland-appearance-unstable-v1
protocol): the entry names and values are identical and must
stay in sync. Any new value must be added to both at once.
